name: agentic-engineering
description: Tools for building software with Claude Code agents — the parts that should not be improvised: how work is handed over, how a worker is stood up and stood down, and how a report is checked before it is believed.

plugins.name: agent-crew
plugins.description: Run a crew of Claude Code worker sessions under one coordinator: start and retire them in cmux panels, clear a worker's context between tasks without losing its identity, write task briefs that survive a context wipe, and verify what comes back. Ships a developer, a read-only tester, and a solution-architect role that shapes the work before anyone implements it.

plugins.name: beads-backlog
plugins.description: The backlog agent-crew's workers pull from, held in Beads. The crew names the moves in the abstract - find existing work, create an item, link a dependency, claim one, close it, record what was learned - and this plugin binds them to `bd`, so a coordinator drives a real store instead of asking which one to use. Swap it for another provider to change store without touching the crew.

plugins.name: madr-decisions
plugins.description: Records decisions in MADR, and keeps them readable as history. Generates the record rather than describing the format, so the shape is never recalled from memory; and supersedes a decision by writing a new one and flipping a single line of the old, because a record rewritten to match today's code destroys the only account of what was decided. Swap it for another format provider without changing how the rest of your tooling refers to it.

plugins.name: peer-review
plugins.description: Get a verdict on work that already exists — a plan, a document, an uncommitted diff, or the current branch's work — from a reviewer deliberately given no context beyond the artifact itself. Read-only: reports defects, leaves the decision to you.

plugins.name: pipeline-watch
plugins.description: Watches for pushes to an open pull request and reacts on its own. When one happens the agent is told to wait for the pipeline, read what it reported about that push, prove the result is not a stale run left over from the commit before, and fix what its own commits introduced - without anybody remembering to ask. Silent on every other command.
